data.title: The hillfort of Žilín near Papradno – the legend of the black dogs
data.excerpt: One more legend, this time attached to the hillfort of Žilín above the village of Papradno – according to the available information a small fort with a triple stone rampart. A brigands' treasure is said to lie hidden there, guarded by three black dogs which drove even the fearless Countess Baláži-Gáborka off the hill.
data.metaTitle: Žilín near Papradno – the legend of the black dogs
data.metaDescription: A legend of the small fort of Žilín with its triple stone rampart above Papradno in the Javorníky — the tale of the black dogs guarding a brigands' treasure.

children.text: I am adding one more legend, this time connected with the hillfort of Žilín, which lies above the village of Papradno. According to the available information it was a small fort with a triple stone rampart.

Deep in the woods of the Javorníky, in one of the upper branches of the Papradno valley, stands the hill of Žilín. From time immemorial it has been a generous home to wild game and a hiding place for bands of brigands. But that is not all. Long, long ago an ancient tribe of the Slavs is said to have had its seat on it, before it moved into the Váh valley, to the territory of present-day Žilina. Some Slavic chieftain built a small timber fort on Žilín, and it long withstood the onslaughts of enemies and of the harsh Javorníky winters, until at last, no one knows why, it was laid in ashes. Perhaps the ancient pagan gods took it ill that their worshippers had abandoned them and given themselves to a new faith, Christianity; perhaps Perún himself sent down thunder and lightning on his forsaken sanctuary and the fort burned to the ground. Its ruins became the seat of a bloodthirsty band of brigands, who sowed terror and misfortune all around. Three brigand captains met on Žilín, summoned up the old pagan deities with a dreadful ritual, signed themselves over to them with their own blood and demanded their help. And so those brigand dogs amassed great treasures and hid them somewhere in the neighbourhood. Then they vanished like mist, and time effaced every trace of their presence – on Žilín and in the wounded souls of their victims. It was said that some unfortunate old woman, when they set upon her and robbed her, cursed them in her death throes. And truly, those were still times when a just curse would now and then come to pass.

And other times came, when the ruler of the Papradno woods was the strange Countess Baláži-Gáborka. She feared neither the forest, nor the wild game, nor even the raging of the elements and of the dark powers that take over the world at night. When she once heard that the Besný hill in the Marikovská valley was a forgotten bastion of the ancient Perún, and that he hurled thunder and lightning there at his former worshippers, she set out for the place at once, hung about the neighbourhood and watched for the moment when the forgotten lord of thunder should begin to rage. She did not have to wait long – a gale rose, black clouds darkened the sun, frightened shepherds drove their flocks headlong to safety. Only Gáborka galloped on her steed over the bare crown of the Besný hill while the thunderer spoke in his booming voice. Lightning rained down on the earth like fiery hail. And the fearless countess stood against the raging elements, the gale tore the clothes from her body, the horse neighed in panic, until at last, stunned by that fury, it turned to flee and carried its rider against her will to safety.

The bold countess also learned of the secret of Žilín, and she trembled with impatience to track it down. Gáborka spent the whole summer in the surroundings of the mysterious hill. Many caught sight of her bathing in the pools of the Žilín brook and afterwards lying naked on the flowery hillside. She questioned the wise old men and old women of the district, diligently pieced together the fragments of the forgotten legend and searched for hidden clues to the treasure.

No, it was not a longing for riches that drove Gáborka, for she had enough of them. But that veil of mystery, the shadow of the mysterious demonic powers that guard the enchanted treasure – that was what would not let her sleep.

And she was already very close. She stayed most often in the clearing at the foot of the hill, where the entrance to the brigands' hiding place was said to be, except that no one knew where exactly, or by what spell that entrance opened. There Gáborka now spent her sunny days, lying in the meadow and musing on who knows what.

And once it was high noon, the sun poured its heat over the whole countryside and from far off came the pealing of bells, from somewhere at the church in Jasenica. The scrub at the edge of the clearing parted and a black brute of a dog with a foaming muzzle and its tongue hanging out came out of the forest. And opposite, on the other side of the meadow, a similar monstrous beast appeared, and a third crawled out from among the trees a little lower down. When they caught sight of the woman's figure, their hackles rose and they began to whine, to howl and to bark furiously. In an instant they were within arm's reach, circling the naked countess, who had leapt up in haste from her bed in the meadow, their tails menacingly stiff, their hackles bristling. They began to press in from one side. Gáborka only sprang aside, barefoot and naked, retreating slowly down the clearing, and the dogs harried her from three sides, baring their teeth and panting angrily with fiery flame. Even the bold countess needed no more; truly, she did not even manage to pick up her clothes from the grass, but took to her bare heels and fled before the pressing monsters. And the dogs kept attacking from three sides, leaving only the fourth free for Gáborka's escape. So she ran as fast as her strength would carry her and did not stop until she reached the hamlet of Majer. Here, within sight of the first houses, the dogs howled wildly one last time and vanished into the woods.
From then on the countess gave Žilín a wide berth and never again searched for its dreadful secret.
